propositions: Canonical `rebar bridge preview` and `rebar bridge sync` subcommands must become the primary vocabulary while legacy `rebar reconcile` remains callable with dry-run default and full backward compatibility.

Legacy `--mode` and `--filter-local-ids` flags must retain their documented behavior (post-differ write filtering) while canonical `--only`/`--except` narrow differ inputs before execution, both reaching the same normalized request path.

Direct engine, Python library `rebar.reconcile()`, MCP `reconcile` tool, and workflows must remain functional with their historical defaults; `reconcile-check` remains lock-free and diagnostic, not collapsed into preview.

Selection tokens in `--only`/`--except` must resolve to existing local IDs or Jira keys before lock acquisition; unresolved, partial, or stale selections exit 2 and never acquire lock or call differ/apply/persist.
Explicit `--max-changes` cap applies deterministic partitions for capped live runs while preserving deterministic applied/deferred manifests; uncapped live and legacy bootstrap remain unchanged.
ADR 0092, compatibility adapters in multiple facades, and every legacy entrypoint (CLI, engine, library, MCP, external-DC helper, workflow) must remain shippable and tested without silent rewrites.
